text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their WWednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The chairman of Lithuania's Social Democratic Party, Aloyzas Sakalas, said he would support his deputy, Vytenis Andriukaitis, in the December presidential election because of his youth. Andiukaitis is 46, while Sakalas is 66.
- Vilniaus Bank's first half audited net profit was 21.7 million litas compared to 11.7 million litas in the same period last year.

- The privatisation commission has approved sell-off programmes for the 87.14 percent state-owned hotel New Vilnius and 60 percent state-run drill producer Graztai. The starting prices will be 15.6 million litas and two million litas respectively.

- About 22 percent of the shares in the Swedish-Lithuanian joint venture Paroc Silikatas, an insulation producer, have been sold to Finland's Partek Insulation. Paroc Silikitas has a 40 share of Lithuania's insulation market.
- Specialists predict that private providers of hot water and heating will undercut municipal and district providers following a 40 percent increase in the price of hot water.
- The economy ministry will institute a loan guarantee fund for small and medium-sized businesses for credits of up to 300,000 litas this year.

- The government is expected to decide on Wednesday on whether to issue state obligations worth 1.745 million litas to Turto Bank so that 78.5 million litas worth of bad laons can be removed from the state-owned Lithuanian State Commericial Bank.
- The government will discuss the establishment of a fund to assist employees of bankrupt companies.

- Lithuania's Social Democratic Party has called on Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius to dismiss the ministers of European affairs, health, interior and the economy and to live up to his party's promise of a "clean hands" policy of governing.

- The government will decide today on the price of shares of a 66 million litas share capital issue by Lithuanian Gas. After the issue the share capital will stand at 437 million litas, of which the state will own 78.04 percent compared to its current 91.08 percent.
- The government will decide on Wednesday whether to stop providing compensation for heat and hot water to low-income families who do not use the subsidies to pay their bills.
